primitives.name: Threshold Weighted Continuous Ranked Probability Score
primitives.verbatim_quote: Equations & assumptions twCRPS(F,y;w) = ∫ w(z)·(F(z) - 1{y≤z})2 dz with w(z) = 1{z > t}.
primitives.latex: \text{twCRPS}(F, y; w) = \int w(z) \cdot (F(z) - \mathbb{1}_{y \leq z})^2 \, dz \quad \text{with } w(z) = \mathbb{1}_{z > t}
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'F(z)': 'Cumulative distribution function (dimensionless)', 'y': 'Observed outcome (wind speed m/s)', 'z': 'Integration variable (wind speed m/s)', 'w(z)': 'Weight function (dimensionless)', 't': 'Threshold value (wind speed m/s)'}
primitives.assumptions: The weight function w(z) is indicator-based for z > t; twCRPS is proper for the weighted functional class.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When w(z) = 0 for all z, reduces to standard CRPS; when w(z) = 1 for z > t, emphasizes tail behavior.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core innovation lies in modifying the Continuous Ranked Probability Score (CRPS) to emphasize extreme outcomes through a threshold-weighted scoring rule (twCRPS). This addresses the fundamental limitation of standard CRPS, which penalizes deviations uniformly across the entire distribution, thereby underweighting extreme events. The twCRPS introduces a weight function w(z) = 1{z > t}, focusing training on outcomes exceeding a high threshold t. This modification allows post-processing models to better capture tail behavior without completely neglecting the body. The trade-off between body and tail performance is managed via linear pooling: F_pool = λ·F_twCRPS + (1−λ)·F_CRPS. With λ=0.6, the model retains ~1.3–2.5% improvement in tail forecasts while minimizing degradation in body accuracy. The EMOS framework provides a flexible parametric structure for probabilistic forecasts, using truncated normal/logistic distributions to ensure physical consistency. The truncation at zero ensures non-negative wind speeds, and seasonal components enhance temporal adaptability. These primitives form a coherent system for tail-sensitive probabilistic forecasting, directly applicable to GSE’s need for blowout and ceiling event prediction.
